section_1.title: Introduction: Beyond 3D Intuition (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Define the n-dimensional sphere (hypersphere) using the equation Σxᵢ² = R². Contrast the 2D circle and 3D sphere to prime the audience for abstraction.
section_1.example: Visualizing a 'slicing' animation where a 3D sphere passes through a 2D plane (becoming a circle), helping students visualize a 4D sphere passing through 3D space.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Review: The Distance Formula (0:45-1:30)
section_2.content: Briefly revisit the Pythagorean theorem and Euclidean distance. Establish that distance in n-dimensions is simply an extension: d = √(x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ²).
section_2.example: A 2D character (Dotty) calculating the distance to a point, then extending the formula to a 3D character (Cube) moving in a room.

section_3.title: The 'Empty' Core Paradox (1:30-2:45)
section_3.content: Discuss the distribution of volume. As dimensions increase, volume migrates from the center to the 'crust' of the sphere. Mathematically show that for very high dimensions, almost all volume lies within an infinitesimally thin shell near the surface.
section_3.example: An orange analogy: As the 'orange' (hypersphere) grows in dimension, the 'peel' (the surface region) holds 99% of the fruit, leaving the center virtually empty.

section_4.title: The Corner Concentration Mystery (2:45-4:15)
section_4.content: Explain that hyperspheres inscribed in a hypercube barely touch the sides, and the 'corners' of the cube become increasingly vast. This explains why high-dimensional data points are often sparse.
section_4.example: A robot trying to navigate a high-dimensional box; it finds that the 'corners' are so far away that it essentially gets lost in the voids, while the sphere stays central.

section_5.title: Real-World Application & Summary (4:15-5:00)
section_5.content: Connect high-dimensional spheres to Data Science (k-Nearest Neighbors) and Machine Learning, where 'distances' behave counter-intuitively in high-dimensional feature spaces.
section_5.example: A search engine algorithm that views each query as a point in a 10,000-dimensional space, using hyperspheres to cluster similar user preferences.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Right side grid: adjust X offset to be in right half (3 to 7)
                x = 3.5 + j * 0.7
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.7
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

        lecture_lines = [
            "Most sphere volume migrates to the shell.",
            "The center becomes hollow as dimensions grow.",
            "Think of an orange with a giant peel.",
            "Almost all mass concentrates near the crust.",
            "Volume shifts away from the inner sphere."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The 'Empty' Core Paradox", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create visual elements
        # 1. Intuitive Hook
        sphere_core = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere_core, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)

        self.place_at_grid(integral_text, 'C5', scale_factor=0.7)

        shell = Ring(inner_radius=1.0, outer_radius=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.6)

        peel = Annulus(inner_radius=1.3, outer_radius=1.5, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=1.0)

        # 5. Summary (99%)

import numpy as np

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
